events.text: Under the quay of Mirrorhold Isle, a keeper named Old Sunle shows you a water-clock that no one built. Its basin fills and empties on no schedule of day or night, and the keeper swears each fill is somebody's hour.

choices.text: Ask whose hour it is counting

effects.log: Sunle shrugs. "Mine, mostly. Today, maybe yours."

choices.text: Watch the basin until it turns

effects.log: It fills in a long slow breath, then drains, and you feel oddly rested.

choices.text: Say clocks should be left alone

effects.log: Sunle laughs, pleased, and offers you tea instead.

events.text: The basin quickens as you stand near it. The water climbs the glass in bright beads, and for a moment you see the quay as it will look in thirty years: older boats, a wider stair, and nobody you know.

choices.text: Look away before it finishes

effects.log: The vision breaks into ordinary dusk. You are glad of the noise of gulls.

choices.text: Hold the gaze to the end

effects.log: It ends on a small quiet scene, someone mending a net, and you carry it with you.

choices.text: Ask Sunle what the clock is for

effects.log: "For being late less often," Sunle says. It is not a joke.

events.text: Sunle falls ill, and the clock stops with a final drop. No one on the isle can restart it. A rival keeper from the Jade Court offers to buy the basin and "manage" it, with offices and fees.

choices.text: Refuse the Court's offer on Sunle's behalf

effects.log: The Court clerk bows stiffly. The isle claps, which is rare.

choices.text: Try to wind the clock yourself

effects.log: You pour in a cup of your own patience and the basin shivers into motion again.

choices.text: Let the Court take it

effects.log: It will be tidy and useless. You tell yourself it will be safe.

events.text: Sunle recovers, thin and cheerful, and the clock fills again at its own pace. On the rim someone has scratched a new mark, a single wave, and Sunle says it was not there yesterday. "It counts you now," the keeper says.

choices.text: Come back each year to see your mark

effects.log: The wave deepens a little each visit, like a friend who remembers.

choices.text: Leave a spirit stone for the upkeep

effects.log: The stone sinks into the basin and the water glows pale blue for a night.

choices.text: Take your leave with a bow

effects.log: You go lighter, as if a small debt had been named and forgiven.

events.text: A gate stands in the cliff face of Hollow Isle, locked all day. At dusk it swings open on a drowsy orchard whose fruit hums softly. A child tending it says the trees only fruit for guests who arrive tired.
events.arc: The Orchard Open Only at Dusk

choices.text: Step through, weary as you are

effects.log: The air smells of plums and warm stone. The child hands you a basket without a word.

choices.text: Ask the child who owns the orchard

effects.log: "The trees do," the child says, as though this were obvious.

choices.text: Wait outside until you can sleep on your feet

effects.log: You are asked in just as you begin to sway. It is the nearest thing to kindness.

events.text: The fruit is plum-gold and sings a single note when you lift it. The child warns you: eat one, and you will sleep until the orchard decides to wake you; take two, and the orchard will remember your face.
events.arc: The Orchard Open Only at Dusk

choices.text: Eat one and sleep

effects.log: You dream of a stair that goes up forever, and wake rested in a way you had forgotten.

choices.text: Take two and risk the memory

effects.log: The orchard exhales. You feel looked at, not unkindly.

choices.text: Take none and just listen

effects.log: The notes layer into a quiet chord. It is enough.

events.text: A guest from the Sea-Cloud Council arrives with an axe-bearing crew, to clear the trees for a landing pier. The child stands in front of the first trunk, very small, and looks at you.
events.arc: The Orchard Open Only at Dusk

choices.text: Stand beside the child

effects.log: The crew hesitates. The foreman reads your standing and calls a halt.

choices.text: Offer the foreman a better pier site

effects.log: You point to a bare ledge half a mile on. It works, grumbling.

choices.text: Say it is not your quarrel

effects.log: The axes lift. You do not stay to watch.

events.text: Dusk again, and the gate opens for you alone. The orchard has put forth a single fruit on a low bough, bright as a lantern, with your name inked on it in a child's hand.
events.arc: The Orchard Open Only at Dusk

choices.text: Eat it under the tree

effects.log: It tastes like being ten years old and forgiven. You sleep, and wake with the whole orchard singing.

choices.text: Plant its seed on another isle

effects.log: A sapling comes up that opens only at dusk. Passers-by call it the strange tree.

choices.text: Leave it for the next tired guest

effects.log: You leave it glowing on the bough and walk away light-handed.

events.text: On the dead edge of Sable Isle stands an observatory whose dome is full of stone moons, thirteen of them, all cracked. A surveyor from the Weather Ministry says each moon once showed a different tide.

choices.text: Climb the dome stair

effects.log: Dust rises in the light. The moons lie in cradles, quiet as eggs.

choices.text: Ask the surveyor what broke them

effects.log: "Time did," says the surveyor, "and a little spite."

choices.text: Sketch the dome and move on

effects.log: The sketch is good enough that the surveyor asks to keep it.

events.text: The thirteenth moon is whole, though small, and when you breathe on it a thin line of light runs round its rim. It shows a tide that is not in this sea: slow, silver, and far deeper.

choices.text: Study the tide it shows

effects.log: You count its swells until your head clears. Something in you matches the rhythm.

choices.text: Show it to the surveyor

effects.log: The surveyor goes pale and writes for an hour without stopping.

choices.text: Cover it with a cloth

effects.log: It is not yours to wake. The light settles slowly.

events.text: The surveyor's ministry sends a party to carry the whole dome off in crates. Their foreman wants the thirteenth moon first, "for safety," and the cradle trembles when he reaches for it.

choices.text: Stop the foreman with a word

effects.log: You tell him what the moon showed. His hand drops.

choices.text: Let the Ministry finish its crating

effects.log: The cradle goes empty with a sound like a held breath.

choices.text: Warn the surveyor in private

effects.log: They arrange a quiet delay with a hundred forms. Bureaucracy, used kindly.

events.text: Months later a crate arrives at your door, unsigned. Inside is the thirteenth moon, cleaned, with a note: "It asked for you." The tide on its rim is slow, silver, and entirely at rest.

choices.text: Keep it by your window

effects.log: On quiet nights you can hear a far-off sea. You sleep deeply.

choices.text: Return it to its cradle on Sable

effects.log: You carry it back, and the broken twelve seem to lean toward it.

choices.text: Pass it to a student of tides

effects.log: They weep and stammer thanks. It is the best gift you ever gave.

events.text: A herd of cloud-elk crosses the Pale Reach each autumn, and one stag among them carries antlers that drip real rain. Hunters of the Gale Quay say nobody has ever laid a hand on it. They want you to try.
events.arc: The Cloud-Elk with Antlers of Rain

choices.text: Join the hunt at the quay

effects.log: You are issued a rope, a lantern, and a stern warning about the weather.

choices.text: Ask what the hunters want it for

effects.log: "The rain," says the captain. "A farm on the Reach has had none for three years."

choices.text: Decline and watch from the cliff

effects.log: The herd moves like a slow river of white. You are glad you came.

events.text: You track the stag through a day of thin mist. Its rain leaves a wet trail on the grass, easy to follow, and at noon you find it drinking from a pool that was dry yesterday.
events.arc: The Cloud-Elk with Antlers of Rain

choices.text: Creep close with the rope ready

effects.log: It lifts its head. Rain falls on your shoulders, cool and smelling of green.

choices.text: Stay hidden and just watch

effects.log: The stag drinks, and the pool grows wider by the minute.

choices.text: Whistle softly to call it

effects.log: It turns an ear. For a long moment you are the only thing in its world.

events.text: The stag turns and walks toward you, unhurried, and stops an arm's length off. Its antlers shake, and the rain falls harder, as though it were asking something. Behind you the hunters are shouting to cast the ropes.
events.arc: The Cloud-Elk with Antlers of Rain

choices.text: Wave the hunters back

effects.log: They grumble but obey. The stag bows its head.

choices.text: Cast the rope as asked

effects.log: The stag leaps and is gone in a gust of wet wind. The rope hangs slack and dripping.

choices.text: Hold out your open hand

effects.log: A single cold drop falls on your palm and stays there, glowing.

events.text: Weeks on, a storm that should have missed the dry farm turns and pours on it for three days. The farmer swears a white stag stood on the ridge through every hour of it. The hunters' captain sends you a flask of rain-water and a small apology.
events.arc: The Cloud-Elk with Antlers of Rain

choices.text: Pour the flask over the farm's well

effects.log: The well rises, sweet and cold. The farm will survive.

choices.text: Drink it yourself

effects.log: It tastes of mountains. For a day you feel like weather.

choices.text: Keep it sealed on a shelf

effects.log: The flask beads with fresh drops whenever you are troubled.

events.text: A roc nested once on the Salt Ledge, and the egg was left behind when the bird flew. A trader named Vessa Lan says it has sat there for forty years, slowly turning white as bone, and she is afraid to touch it.
events.arc: The Roc Egg on the Salt Ledge

choices.text: Offer to climb to the ledge

effects.log: The path is a narrow wet rib of rock. Vessa ties your boots for you.

choices.text: Ask why the roc left it

effects.log: "Because it was the wrong season," says Vessa. "Or because the bird was afraid."

choices.text: Suggest the Ministry send a crew

effects.log: Vessa makes a face. "They would put it in a museum."

events.text: The egg is the size of a hut and warm to the touch. Inside, something stirs slowly, like a sleeper rolling over. Gulls watch you from every ledge, unusually quiet.
events.arc: The Roc Egg on the Salt Ledge

choices.text: Sit with the egg through the night

effects.log: You lean on it for warmth. The stirring slows to match your breath.

choices.text: Sing it a lullaby

effects.log: You know only one and it is badly out of tune. The egg seems to approve.

choices.text: Knock three times, politely

effects.log: There is a long pause. Something inside knocks back, once.

events.text: At dawn the shell cracks along a single clean line and a wet, enormous, deeply offended chick glares at you. It is hungry, and the Salt Ledge has nothing but salt.
events.arc: The Roc Egg on the Salt Ledge

choices.text: Run back to Vessa for fish

effects.log: You return with three baskets. The chick eats like a landslide.

choices.text: Carry the chick to a fishing isle

effects.log: It rides on your shoulders, impossibly heavy, and the isle folk gape.

choices.text: Call the Ministry's beast-wardens

effects.log: They arrive with a basket of nets. The chick eyes you in betrayal.

events.text: A year later a shadow crosses the sun and the sea goes dark under wings. The roc, grown to the size of a small isle, lands on the ledge, tilts its great head, and leaves a single gold feather at your feet before taking flight.
events.arc: The Roc Egg on the Salt Ledge

choices.text: Keep the feather in a cloth

effects.log: It sings faintly in a wind. Travel is a little easier from then on.

choices.text: Give it to Vessa for her trade

effects.log: She weeps and sells it for a fair price, and gives you half.

choices.text: Hang it above the Gale Quay gate

effects.log: Every boat that passes under it is lucky for a season.

events.text: Beneath the White Stairs of Orin Isle, a cave echoes with low chords. A scholar named Ninfa Weise explains that the stones in the walls were carved by an old hand to hold books, in tones, not letters.

choices.text: Press an ear to a stone

effects.log: The note is slow and heavy as a bell under water. A sentence forms, almost.

choices.text: Hum back at it

effects.log: Several stones answer in tune. Ninfa looks delighted and alarmed.

choices.text: Ask Ninfa to read one aloud

effects.log: "Not read," Ninfa says. "Sing. But we have only one person who can."

events.text: Ninfa's one singer is an old cook called Pao, who learned the scale from her grandmother for a lullaby. She sings a stone for you: a recipe for rain-pickled lotus, in four-part harmony, grave as a hymn.

choices.text: Ask Pao to sing a different stone

effects.log: It is a boundary line between two long-dead farms. Pao weeps a little.

choices.text: Learn the scale yourself

effects.log: It takes a week. You hum for a month afterward.

choices.text: Thank Pao and bring her tea

effects.log: She is touched out of all proportion. She will sing for you, now, forever.

events.text: A deep stone at the cave's back resists every singer. Ninfa thinks it holds the library's catalogue, and that if it speaks, the whole wall will wake. The Jade Court has sent a clerk to watch, and the clerk is plainly counting fees.

choices.text: Sing the stone with Pao

effects.log: Your two voices lift and the stone answers in a deep dry bass, listing a thousand titles.

choices.text: Warn Ninfa of the Court's interest

effects.log: Ninfa nods and starts hiding the best stones behind a false wall.

choices.text: Let the clerk make an inventory

effects.log: The clerk writes, bored, until the wall begins to hum. The clerk stops writing.

events.text: The wall wakes, one stone after another, and the cave rings like a cathedral. Ninfa weeps and keeps a tally. Among the titles is one that names you, or someone with your name, as "the one who listens."

choices.text: Ask the stones what that means

effects.log: They sing a soft, slow answer you will puzzle over for a decade.

choices.text: Hold the note and let it fade

effects.log: The cave settles. The library has chosen to be quiet again.

choices.text: Help Ninfa found a school of singers

effects.log: It takes years, and the school is small and warm and loud.

events.text: The face of Needle Cliff is climbed by threads, long silver cables spun by a colony of cloud-spiders, and the climbers who ride them are a quiet guild of weavers. A guild-mother named Taizhi lets you watch at dawn.

choices.text: Ask to climb with them

effects.log: Taizhi laughs and ties you to a thread. "Do not look down. Do not look up either."

choices.text: Watch the spiders spin

effects.log: They drift out in slow spirals. Each thread glints like a held note.

choices.text: Buy a coil of thread for the road

effects.log: Taizhi sells you a small coil, light as hair and strong as a vow.

events.text: Halfway up the cliff the thread hums and shivers. A ledge opens, and on it a tiny garden grows where no soil should be, full of white flowers that lean toward you. Taizhi says nobody has found it before.

choices.text: Tend the garden for an hour

effects.log: You pull a few weeds and find the roots are made of thread.

choices.text: Pick one flower

effects.log: It folds as you hold it, then glows softly. It will not wilt.

choices.text: Mark the spot for the guild

effects.log: Taizhi nods in approval. The garden will be tended.

events.text: At the summit a storm builds fast, and the threads begin to sing. Taizhi shouts that you must unclip and climb down by hand. The guild's younger climbers are scattered on the face and they are frightened.

choices.text: Help the youngest climbers down

effects.log: You pass them from ledge to ledge, calling the holds. All are safe.

choices.text: Anchor the thread for the others

effects.log: You take the full strain on your arms. It leaves you shaking but they come down.

choices.text: Climb down first and shout directions

effects.log: It works, but not all of them are grateful afterward.

events.text: After the storm the guild gathers at the base of the cliff. Taizhi weaves a short silver cord and ties it round your wrist. "You may climb any thread of ours," the guild-mother says. "The cliff knows you now."

choices.text: Wear the cord with pride

effects.log: On windy days it tightens, a gentle hand on your arm.

choices.text: Teach a young climber to read weather

effects.log: It is the best use of the cord. The youngster goes far.

choices.text: Tie the cord to your door-latch

effects.log: The house hums softly in a gale, never rattling.

events.text: A lake on Willow Isle shows no reflection: looking in, you see not the sky above but a second sky below, with its own clouds drifting the wrong way. A ferryman, Hodo Krell, says swimmers who dive in come out the other side.
events.arc: The Lake Whose Floor Is Sky

choices.text: Ask where the other side is

effects.log: "Wherever you meant to be," says Hodo. "Rarely where you needed."

choices.text: Lean over the water and look

effects.log: Your face does not appear. A faint bird crosses the lower sky.

choices.text: Hire Hodo's ferry across

effects.log: The boat seems to hang in air. It is oddly calming.

events.text: Mid-lake, Hodo ships his oars and lets the boat drift. Below, the lower sky is crowded with floating isles, none of them on any chart. A lantern sways on the nearest, as though someone were waiting.
events.arc: The Lake Whose Floor Is Sky

choices.text: Dive for the lower isle

effects.log: You fall through cold light and land softly on a lawn of grey moss.

choices.text: Wave at the lantern

effects.log: It swings twice. Somebody below waves back.

choices.text: Row on and leave it be

effects.log: You cross the lake. The lower sky follows you like a patient dog.

events.text: On the lower isle you meet a widow, Brisa Maul, who has kept the lantern lit for her husband's ferry for nine years. He drowned crossing, and the sky below took him in. She asks whether you saw any boat.
events.arc: The Lake Whose Floor Is Sky

choices.text: Tell her what you saw, and what you did not

effects.log: She nods, grateful for the plain truth. She makes you tea.

choices.text: Say you saw a boat, and lie kindly

effects.log: It costs you something. She sleeps that night for the first time in years.

choices.text: Offer to carry a letter up

effects.log: She writes one. It takes her till dawn.

events.text: You carry Brisa's letter to the world above, to a ferryman's grave on Willow Isle, and read it aloud there. The wind rises and the lake ripples as though turning a page. A boat you have never seen rocks gently at the dock for a night and is gone by morning.
events.arc: The Lake Whose Floor Is Sky

choices.text: Leave a lantern at the dock

effects.log: It burns until the next dusk. Hodo says that is a good sign.

choices.text: Sit beside the grave until sunrise

effects.log: You are sure you have done a small and right thing.

choices.text: Tell Brisa, by letter, that it arrived

effects.log: Her answer comes in two seasons, in a steady hand: thank you.

events.text: A cloud-whale called Old Grandmother surfaces off the Southern Reach with a whole harbour on her back: docks, warehouses, even a small market, all grown over with pearl-grass. Nobody built it. A harbour-master, Lio Fen, claims it as hers.
events.arc: The Whale That Carried a Harbour

choices.text: Ask Lio to show you the harbour

effects.log: She leads you along planks that rock with the whale's slow breath.

choices.text: Greet the whale respectfully

effects.log: A great eye opens, patient and vast. It closes again.

choices.text: Ask what the harbour was for

effects.log: "Trade," Lio says. "And hiding. Every harbour is both."

events.text: Under the market planks you find a hold full of crates sealed with a mark no guild owns. Lio says the whale has carried them for centuries, and every year a few more appear. She has never opened one.
events.arc: The Whale That Carried a Harbour

choices.text: Open a crate

effects.log: Inside lie bolts of cloud-silk, quite fresh, with a note from a trader long dead.

choices.text: Leave them all sealed

effects.log: Lio exhales. Some things keep better closed.

choices.text: Ask the whale who loaded them

effects.log: A deep note rolls up through the planks. It is not a word, but you feel the answer.

events.text: A ministry cutter arrives with orders to tow the whale to a proper port. The captain is polite and immovable. Lio cries that the harbour will be taken apart.
events.arc: The Whale That Carried a Harbour

choices.text: Argue the whale's case before the captain

effects.log: You cite three old treaties. The captain pauses, then radios the Ministry.

choices.text: Rouse the harbour folk to sing

effects.log: Old Grandmother answers. The cutter's hull hums in sympathy and falls back.

choices.text: Slip a petition to the Weather Ministry

effects.log: It takes weeks, but the cutter is recalled.

events.text: Years on, Old Grandmother passes the Southern Reach again and Lio hails you from the dock, now with a new roof, three goats, and a crate she finally opened. It held an old compass that points not north but to home. She presses it into your hands.
events.arc: The Whale That Carried a Harbour

choices.text: Take the compass

effects.log: On long roads it never fails to turn gently toward the people you have loved.

choices.text: Give it back to the whale's hold

effects.log: The crate is resealed with a quiet bow. The whale hums.

choices.text: Ask Lio to keep it for the harbour

effects.log: She weeps, and the harbour becomes a little more like a home.

events.text: Past the last inhabited isle, a rail of black iron runs along the lip of the world with nothing beyond it but wind. A guard named Yannick Dorr keeps it clean. Beyond it, he says, something keeps knocking.
events.arc: The Last Rail at the Edge of the Isles

choices.text: Lean on the rail and listen

effects.log: The wind carries a faint rhythm, patient and slow.

choices.text: Ask Yannick why he guards it

effects.log: "Someone should be here," he says. "In case it answers."

choices.text: Tap the rail twice in reply

effects.log: The knocking stops. After a moment it taps twice back.

events.text: The knocking comes from a ship, hull-down below the edge, hanging by long chains from a cloud. Its lanterns are lit and its crew are asleep at their posts. Yannick says it has hung there since his grandfather's day.
events.arc: The Last Rail at the Edge of the Isles

choices.text: Climb down the chains

effects.log: Each link is cold and slick. The ship swings gently as you land.

choices.text: Hail the ship with a lantern

effects.log: A bell on board answers. Nothing else moves.

choices.text: Warn Yannick it may be a trap

effects.log: He nods thoughtfully. "It has been waiting for company. Not necessarily for harm."

events.text: On the deck sleep eleven sailors, still breathing, locked in a long dream. A single empty hammock hangs among them. The captain's log says the ship was sailing to the edge to find a new isle, and was held here by a wish.
events.arc: The Last Rail at the Edge of the Isles

choices.text: Take the empty hammock and sleep

effects.log: You dream of the isle they sought, green and breathing. You wake with a plan.

choices.text: Wake the sailors one by one

effects.log: They stir groggily, thanking you before they remember who they are.

choices.text: Read the captain's log aloud

effects.log: The sailors murmur in their sleep, as if to a lullaby.

events.text: The ship turns on its chains and swings free into the wind, sails filling. The sailors wave from the rail and the knocking ceases. Yannick stands at the last rail with tears on his face and a cup of tea he has forgotten to drink.
events.arc: The Last Rail at the Edge of the Isles

choices.text: Wave until the ship is a speck

effects.log: The sky is very wide. You feel unexpectedly part of it.

choices.text: Join Yannick for a quiet cup

effects.log: The two of you sit at the rail until stars come out.

choices.text: Carve a mark on the rail for the crew

effects.log: The iron takes it softly. Someone will see it.

events.text: In the eye of the Ninefold Storm sits an island of weaving frames, tended by a woman called Eshe Quar. Her loom turns winds into bolts of cloth, and she is looking for an apprentice who is not afraid of thunder.

choices.text: Offer to hold the shuttle

effects.log: It is cold and shaped like a bird. It hums when you grip it.

choices.text: Ask what the cloth is for

effects.log: "Calming," Eshe says. "A town can sleep under it for a decade."

choices.text: Watch a gust become a thread

effects.log: It slides between her fingers, white then silver then gone.

events.text: Eshe lets you try a small pattern: three rows of pale cloud-wool, a knot, and a turn. Your thread keeps fraying in the wind. She smiles and says the wind is testing your patience, not your skill.

choices.text: Slow your breath and weave again

effects.log: The thread holds. A tiny square of calm settles over the frame.

choices.text: Weave with song

effects.log: The wind pauses to listen. The pattern is crooked and very beautiful.

choices.text: Ask Eshe to show you how

effects.log: She does, wordlessly, and your hands learn faster than you do.

events.text: A cutter of the Weather Ministry arrives with orders to buy the loom. Their offer is generous, and they promise the cloth will protect the whole fleet. Eshe is tempted, and tired, and looks to you.

choices.text: Advise Eshe to keep her loom

effects.log: She nods slowly. The cutter goes away with an order for one bolt only.

choices.text: Advise Eshe to sell and rest

effects.log: She does. The fleet sleeps safely, and Eshe sleeps too.

choices.text: Offer to learn the loom first

effects.log: Eshe teaches you the rest of the pattern over a long, loud week.

events.text: The final bolt is yours: a grey and silver cloth that lies still in a gale. Eshe wraps it round your shoulders and says the Ninefold Storm will let you pass whenever you wear it. "It does not forgive being forgotten," she adds.

choices.text: Wear it and walk into the storm

effects.log: The wind parts like a curtain. The storm looks at you and lets you by.

choices.text: Gift it to a hamlet in the storm's path

effects.log: Down in the mortal world below, a long wet season ends gently.

choices.text: Keep it folded for a day of need

effects.log: It stays folded for years, faintly humming.

events.text: A pattern of nine stars hangs over Yarrow Isle every autumn, and this year it has only eight. An old stargazer, Pell Imre, is out of sorts about it. "I have named the ninth for sixty years," he says. "I do not know what to do with a gap."
events.arc: The Constellation That Lost a Star

choices.text: Help him chart the gap

effects.log: You spend a night with ink and a lens. The gap is perfectly round.

choices.text: Ask where a star goes when it leaves

effects.log: "Out, usually," says Pell. "Or down."

choices.text: Offer to climb the watch-tower for a closer look

effects.log: The stair is long. The view is, for once, worth it.

events.text: From the tower you see a faint glow in the ravine below the isle, as if the star had fallen into a stream. Pell insists stars do not fall. He says this while lacing his boots.
events.arc: The Constellation That Lost a Star

choices.text: Descend the ravine with Pell

effects.log: The stream is cold and bright. Something small glimmers on its bed.

choices.text: Send a lantern down on a line

effects.log: The lantern swings and lights a circle of pale shells.

choices.text: Wait until dawn to see what remains

effects.log: By dawn the glow is a handful of pearl-dust on wet stone.

events.text: In the stream lies a very small star, no bigger than a hazelnut, dimmed and shivering. It brightens a little as you cup it. Pell says that stars do not live down here, and that it will not last the week.
events.arc: The Constellation That Lost a Star

choices.text: Carry it up to the tower

effects.log: It brightens with every flight of stairs.

choices.text: Warm it in your hands overnight

effects.log: You do not sleep. At dawn it is the size of a coin and humming.

choices.text: Ask the sky to take it back

effects.log: You hold it to the night. It does not rise. It is waiting for something.

events.text: You and Pell lift the star on a kite of white silk, line after line, until the string runs out. The star leaves your kite with a soft pop and rejoins the pattern. Nine stars again. Pell, who has not wept in decades, weeps, loudly.
events.arc: The Constellation That Lost a Star

choices.text: Stay with Pell until sunrise

effects.log: You share tea and a long silence.

choices.text: Chart the pattern with its ninth star restored

effects.log: Your chart is clear and handsome. The observatories ask for copies.

choices.text: Name the ninth star after the stream

effects.log: Pell approves. It stays in the sky forever.

events.text: A rope bridge across the Silver Gap has a toll-house with no toll-keeper, only a sign: sing a verse to cross. Behind the house sits a retired ferrier named Ashok Penn, who says the bridge likes tunes that nobody has heard.
events.arc: The Bridge Toll Paid in Songs

choices.text: Sing a lullaby you half remember

effects.log: The ropes hum. The bridge accepts it without comment.

choices.text: Make up a verse about the gap

effects.log: The bridge creaks approvingly and the planks seem to straighten.

choices.text: Pay Ashok in stones instead

effects.log: He shakes his head. "The bridge will not take stones."

events.text: Midway across, the bridge lengthens: each plank you pass stretches a little, as if to keep you in song. A voice from below joins in, deep and unhurried. The gap, apparently, has been waiting for a duet.
events.arc: The Bridge Toll Paid in Songs

choices.text: Sing back to the voice below

effects.log: The harmony rises through the ropes and you feel it in your teeth.

choices.text: Hum quietly and keep walking

effects.log: The voice lowers politely until you are across.

choices.text: Ask the voice who it is

effects.log: It answers with the first verse of a song nobody has sung in a thousand years.

events.text: On the far side a crowd of travellers waits, none of whom can sing. Ashok has collected a pile of coins and promises over the years but they will not do. A young merchant weeps that she cannot carry a tune.
events.arc: The Bridge Toll Paid in Songs

choices.text: Teach the merchant a verse

effects.log: It takes an hour and a great deal of kindness. She crosses.

choices.text: Sing for the whole crowd at once

effects.log: The bridge, startled, lets them all through in a long line.

choices.text: Suggest they wait for another day

effects.log: Ashok frowns. The bridge creaks a little sadly.

events.text: At dusk Ashok announces he is old and tired of keeping the toll-house, and that the bridge has chosen you. He gives you a wooden whistle and the sign. "Whatever you sing," he says, "it will remember."
events.arc: The Bridge Toll Paid in Songs

choices.text: Accept the toll-house for a season

effects.log: You teach the first travellers to hum. The bridge is happier than it has been in years.

choices.text: Take the whistle and decline the house

effects.log: Ashok nods. "Fair." The whistle plays only in your hands.

choices.text: Propose a rota among the travellers

effects.log: It works for a decade. Tunes accumulate like leaves.

events.text: Past the Plum Terraces rises a spring that tastes different to everyone: sour to the greedy, sweet to the generous. A keeper called Rua Hesper has watched it for forty years and says it is, mostly, a polite judge.

choices.text: Drink and see how it tastes

effects.log: It is faintly sweet, with a stranger note beneath. You do not ask what that is.

choices.text: Ask Rua how it decides

effects.log: "It does not decide," says Rua. "It remembers. You just taste what you were."

choices.text: Pour a cup for a passing stranger

effects.log: The stranger tastes it and goes quiet. They leave a coin on the rim.

events.text: The spring begins to bubble harder, and its water turns a pale, uneasy gold. Rua says it does this when someone nearby is about to make a choice that matters. All eyes turn to a thin man in a good coat, who is trembling.

choices.text: Ask the man what is wrong

effects.log: He is a clerk. He has found a sum in the ledgers that does not match.

choices.text: Pour him a cup

effects.log: He drinks. His face clears. He knows what he must do.

choices.text: Watch quietly from a distance

effects.log: The water calms by degrees as he leaves.

events.text: The clerk returns a week later with a Court inspector in tow. Their ledgers have been tampered with by a ring of stone-brokers. The clerk's testimony will cost him his post. He asks for your advice at the spring, with Rua listening.

choices.text: Tell him to speak the truth

effects.log: He does. The brokers are called to account and the clerk is moved to a better post.

choices.text: Advise caution and a witness

effects.log: He finds one. The case holds, slowly.

choices.text: Say it is his choice and no one else's

effects.log: He nods and drinks. The water is sweet.

events.text: The spring runs gold for a full night in your honour, and in the morning Rua hands you a small flask. "Whoever drinks from this will remember what they once forgot," the keeper says. "Use it kindly."

choices.text: Keep the flask for an old friend

effects.log: Years on, you give it to someone who needs it. Their eyes brighten.

choices.text: Drink it yourself

effects.log: A memory returns that you had lost: a morning on a hill, a promise. It warms you.

choices.text: Pour it back into the spring

effects.log: The water shimmers, then settles. Rua nods, pleased.

events.text: On Frost Peak lives a hermit named Orrin Ash, who borrows winter from the lowland isles and keeps it in jars in a cave. In exchange the lowlands get a soft, perfect spring. Lately the jars are running low.
events.arc: The Hermit and the Borrowed Winter

choices.text: Climb the long path to the cave

effects.log: It takes a day, and the air thins. The hermit is waiting at the mouth.

choices.text: Ask how winter is borrowed

effects.log: "By asking," Orrin says. "Winter is lonely, and likes to be invited."

choices.text: Carry a jar down for a hamlet

effects.log: The jar is heavy and cold. It leaves a trail of frost.

events.text: In the cave the jars glow pale blue, each labelled in a spidery hand with the name of a lowland isle. Orrin says Marrow Isle has asked for too much winter, and now its jar is empty and its fields are cracking.
events.arc: The Hermit and the Borrowed Winter

choices.text: Ask Orrin to lend more winter

effects.log: He frowns. "Winter must be returned or it turns sour."

choices.text: Offer to carry a jar to Marrow Isle

effects.log: He sighs, then hands you the largest one with a warning.

choices.text: Suggest the isle plant frost-barley

effects.log: Orrin raises a brow. "That might actually work."

events.text: On Marrow Isle the farmers stand around the cracked fields, sullen. They want their winter back in one night, not by the jarful. You open the jar and cold pours out in a slow white tide.
events.arc: The Hermit and the Borrowed Winter

choices.text: Spread it across the fields slowly

effects.log: Frost settles gently. The soil drinks, and the cracks close.

choices.text: Let the farmers pour it themselves

effects.log: They overdo it and half the barley freezes. They laugh anyway.

choices.text: Save a measure for the next dry year

effects.log: The farmers grumble. You label the jar in their own hand.

events.text: Orrin climbs down from his cave for the first time in forty years to see the green Marrow fields, and weeps. He gives you the smallest jar from his shelf: a winter that fits in a thimble, which will never freeze and never thaw.
events.arc: The Hermit and the Borrowed Winter

choices.text: Keep the thimble of winter

effects.log: On the hottest days you take a sip. It refreshes you for hours.

choices.text: Give it to Marrow Isle's eldest

effects.log: She laughs and sets it on a windowsill. The isle is cooler than before.

choices.text: Pour it into a lake to cool the summer

effects.log: The lake sparkles. Fish rise that nobody has seen before.

events.text: A junior clerk named Faustin Rue stops you at the foot of the Ministries' marble steps and whispers about a back stair: a spiral nobody uses, behind a filing cabinet, that goes somewhere the plans do not show.
events.arc: The Back Stair of the Celestial Ministries

choices.text: Follow Faustin to the cabinet

effects.log: He slides it aside with a practised nudge. Cold air breathes up the dark.

choices.text: Ask who made the stair

effects.log: "The Ministries," Faustin says, "before they decided to forget it."

choices.text: Warn Faustin that clerks are watched

effects.log: He smiles thinly. "That is the other reason I am asking you."

events.text: The stair winds down through dim archives stacked with abandoned petitions, thousands of them, each tied with a red ribbon. Some are a century old. Faustin says they are all requests the Ministries ruled "too small to grant."
events.arc: The Back Stair of the Celestial Ministries

choices.text: Read a petition aloud

effects.log: It is a child's plea for a lantern for a lonely lighthouse.

choices.text: Search for the oldest

effects.log: It asks for rain. It is addressed to a minister who has long retired.

choices.text: Count them with Faustin

effects.log: You stop at four thousand. The room stretches on.

events.text: You and Faustin start granting petitions quietly, one at a time: a lantern here, a rain-cloud there, a bridge repaired by a night-crew. The archive empties by dozens, and a whisper begins in the Ministries that somebody is working nights.
events.arc: The Back Stair of the Celestial Ministries

choices.text: Keep it secret and keep going

effects.log: Months pass. A hundred small needs are met in anonymity.

choices.text: Tell a sympathetic minister

effects.log: She smiles and signs a stack of forms, grim and amused.

choices.text: Pay a stone or two toward the larger requests

effects.log: The stones go further than you expected.

events.text: One evening the back stair is lit end to end, and a retired minister stands on the landing in a faded robe. "I wrote the rule about too small," he says, "and I have regretted it for forty years." He hands you a seal. "Use this to grant the rest."
events.arc: The Back Stair of the Celestial Ministries

choices.text: Use the seal for the lonely requests

effects.log: The last petitions are granted in a night. The archive is empty.

choices.text: Hand the seal to Faustin

effects.log: He holds it as though it were a baby. The Ministries are a little kinder, after that.

choices.text: Decline, and bow to the old minister

effects.log: He nods. "That is exactly what I would have done," he says, and keeps the seal.

events.text: Every spring the herb-pickers of Tallow Hill race up the slope to find the first dew-silver bloom, and the winner is fed on honey and song for a week. A young picker named Ibsen Doh begs you to be his second.
events.arc: The Herb-Pickers' Race on Tallow Hill

choices.text: Agree to be his second

effects.log: You carry the water and the nerves. He grins like a flag.

choices.text: Race on your own account

effects.log: The hill is steep and the other pickers are wiry as goats.

choices.text: Watch from the stand

effects.log: The slope blossoms with colour as they run.

events.text: Halfway up, the slope splits into nine paths, and the bloom could be at the end of any. Ibsen's rival, a stern woman called Mavro Quill, has bribed a guide to point her the right way. You see it happen.
events.arc: The Herb-Pickers' Race on Tallow Hill

choices.text: Call out the bribe publicly

effects.log: The judges halt the race. Mavro glares and is disqualified.

choices.text: Tell Ibsen quietly and let him decide

effects.log: He is angry, then thoughtful. He takes the long path anyway.

choices.text: Do nothing and follow the rival

effects.log: You find the bloom with her, and she says nothing, and neither do you.

events.text: The dew-silver bloom stands in a hollow at the summit, a single flower the colour of morning. Ibsen reaches it first, and offers it to you, a little shy. The judges, the pickers and half the hill wait to see what you do.
events.arc: The Herb-Pickers' Race on Tallow Hill

choices.text: Tell him it is his to win

effects.log: He cries, then laughs. The hill roars for him.

choices.text: Share the bloom, petal by petal

effects.log: The crowd cheers a generous tie. The honey is shared too.

choices.text: Pocket a single petal for luck

effects.log: It brings you a decade of fair weather.

events.text: A fox made of mist haunts Lantern Quay, stealing the paper lanterns of the night-market and carrying them to some den unseen. The market wardens have had enough, and want a hunter. They offer you a small purse of stones.

choices.text: Take the job

effects.log: The wardens give you a bell, a net, and a tired smile.

choices.text: Ask why the fox takes lanterns

effects.log: "For company," says an old stall-keeper. "Probably."

choices.text: Offer to talk to the fox

effects.log: The wardens laugh. Then they stop laughing.

events.text: You follow the fox through the market as it slips between stalls, taking one lantern at a time. At last it leaps a wall and you find its den: a hollow under the quay, full of lanterns, all lit, arranged in a ring like a tiny hamlet.

choices.text: Step into the ring

effects.log: The fox watches from the dark, ears flat. It is deeply, wholly afraid.

choices.text: Bring it a fresh lantern

effects.log: It sniffs the offering and takes it gently.

choices.text: Hold the net but do not throw

effects.log: The fox relaxes by inches, never looking away.

events.text: The wardens come looking for you, and the fox bolts. A little girl at the edge of the ring explains that she has been feeding it: it lost its mist-mother in a storm, and the lanterns are the only thing it understands. She begs you not to take it.

choices.text: Take the girl's side before the wardens

effects.log: You argue the lanterns will be paid for. They grumble and agree.

choices.text: Build the fox a proper lantern-house

effects.log: It moves in within the week and lights it each dusk.

choices.text: Pay the wardens from your purse

effects.log: The purse is lighter and the fox is free.

events.text: On the Gale Road, a guild of kite-hunters chases storm-fish, great silver fish that swim the wind, using kites of oiled silk. A captain, Daro Bell, short a hand, offers you the third line.
events.arc: The Kite-Hunters of the Gale Road

choices.text: Take the third line

effects.log: It is thin and cold, humming with tension.

choices.text: Ask what a storm-fish is worth

effects.log: "A season's peace," says Daro. "And a feast."

choices.text: Admire the kites and decline

effects.log: They are painted with eyes. They seem to watch you.

events.text: A storm-fish takes the bait and drags your line across the sky. The kite bucks and sings. Daro shouts to ease, ease, ease, and you feel the whole sea of air pull on your arms.
events.arc: The Kite-Hunters of the Gale Road

choices.text: Ease the line slowly

effects.log: The fish tires. You gain a yard, then ten.

choices.text: Pull hard and win it fast

effects.log: The line snaps with a crack. The fish is gone and your arms ache.

choices.text: Sing to the fish

effects.log: It slows, listening. Daro stares.

events.text: The fish comes down on the deck, vast and silver, and its eye is wise. Daro says storm-fish carry the memory of every gale they have swum. If released, it will tell the winds who spared it. If kept, it will feed a fleet for a month.
events.arc: The Kite-Hunters of the Gale Road

choices.text: Release the fish

effects.log: It rises and the wind around the Gale Road softens for a season.

choices.text: Share it with the fleet

effects.log: The feast is merry and loud. You eat more than you meant to.

choices.text: Take a single scale as a keepsake

effects.log: It is warm and sings in a gale. The fish bows as it leaves.

events.text: At Cinderfall a falling star once melted a whole orchard into glass, and the trees still stand in their ranks, clear and shining. A caretaker named Nova Lef sweeps the paths and tells you not to touch the leaves.

choices.text: Walk the glass paths quietly

effects.log: Light sifts through the leaves in colours you have no names for.

choices.text: Ask what the garden remembers

effects.log: "Every season it ever had," Nova says. "All at once."

choices.text: Touch a leaf anyway

effects.log: It rings softly. Nova pretends not to see.

events.text: At the heart of the garden grows one tree that is not glass but alive, with green leaves and a trunk wrapped in a ribbon of light. Nova says it grew from a seed that survived the fall, and that it is shy.

choices.text: Sit beneath it

effects.log: It shades you gently. A bird you cannot see begins to sing.

choices.text: Water it from your flask

effects.log: The leaves tremble with something like thanks.

choices.text: Ask Nova how to help it grow

effects.log: "Be quiet near it," she says. "Mostly that."

events.text: A trader from the Jade Exchange offers Nova a fortune for a cutting of glass leaves. Nova refuses; the trader leaves a purse on the gate for you to deliver, hoping you will change her mind. The living tree rustles, as though listening.

choices.text: Give Nova the purse and say nothing

effects.log: She weighs it and hands it back. "No," she says gently.

choices.text: Return the purse to the trader

effects.log: He frowns, then laughs. The garden is left alone.

choices.text: Take a cutting of the living tree to propagate

effects.log: Nova is furious, then relieved. A second tree is planted on a safer isle.

events.text: The Humming Hills of Marrow Isle sing a low chord whenever the sun sets, and shepherds say the sheep graze better to music. A shepherd, Loreto Vance, invites you to sit on the highest knoll to hear it.

choices.text: Sit on the knoll

effects.log: The grass vibrates beneath you. It is not unpleasant.

choices.text: Ask what makes the sound

effects.log: "The hills," says Loreto. "Nobody has asked them why."

choices.text: Hum along

effects.log: The chord deepens. The sheep lift their heads.

events.text: The chord falters one evening, a note missing, and the sheep wander off the slopes in confusion. Loreto says a stone in the northern hill has cracked, and that someone must patch it with a song of the right pitch.

choices.text: Sing the missing note

effects.log: You find it after three tries. The hill answers in kind.

choices.text: Search for the cracked stone

effects.log: You find it half buried in thyme, and fit a clay wedge beside it.

choices.text: Gather the sheep first

effects.log: Loreto thanks you wordlessly and leads the flock back.

events.text: The hills sing whole again, and by morning the slopes are green and the sheep are calm. Loreto gives you a shepherd's whistle carved from hill-bone and says that whenever you play it, the hills will remember you.

choices.text: Keep the whistle

effects.log: It plays only a single note, but it is always the right one.

choices.text: Give it to the next lost traveller

effects.log: The traveller finds their way home. You never learn who.

choices.text: Play it on the highest knoll at dusk

effects.log: The hills answer with a long, warm chord. You sleep under it.

events.text: On Orrery Isle stands the broken tower of an old courier service, whose messengers once rode cloud-horses across the Reach. A historian, Teodora Quint, is collecting letters left in the walls, and asks you to help climb.

choices.text: Climb with Teodora

effects.log: The stair crumbles in places. The view from the top is vast.

choices.text: Ask what the letters say

effects.log: "Mostly bills," she says. "And some love."

choices.text: Help her catalogue below

effects.log: You sort envelopes by the hour, humming.

events.text: In a locked drawer, Teodora finds a letter never delivered, addressed to a girl on a distant isle. It is dated three hundred years ago. It is from a boy who promised to come back, and tells her where he would wait.

choices.text: Offer to trace the address

effects.log: Teodora is delighted. The isle is still on the charts.

choices.text: Read the letter again, quietly

effects.log: It is gentle and rather clumsy. You smile.

choices.text: Suggest burying it with the boy

effects.log: Teodora hesitates, then agrees it should find its girl first.

events.text: You and Teodora carry the letter to the distant isle and learn the girl's line lives on in a tea-house. A great-granddaughter reads the letter aloud over the counter and the whole room goes quiet. The boy never came back, but the girl, she says, kept waiting.

choices.text: Stay for tea and hear the family's tale

effects.log: It is long and warm, and no one leaves hungry.

choices.text: Leave the letter in its hands and slip out

effects.log: You walk to the dock under a fresh sky.

choices.text: Help Teodora publish the tower's other letters

effects.log: It becomes a small beloved book.

events.text: A tea-house on stilts walks the Reach on legs of mist, and appears on a new isle each night. Patrons say its brew is exactly what each drinker needs. Tonight it settles at the edge of your path, steam curling from its door.

choices.text: Step inside for a cup

effects.log: The room is warm and unexpectedly quiet. A bowl of tea steams on a low table.

choices.text: Ask the host who built the house

effects.log: "No one," says the host, a calm young person with ink-stained fingers. "It grew."

choices.text: Sit on the porch and watch the sky

effects.log: The house hums under you, happy.

events.text: The tea tastes different from the way you expect: of an old street, of a cold morning, of a person you stopped writing to. The host says the house brews what is missing. You find you are missing more than you knew.

choices.text: Ask for a second bowl

effects.log: It is bitter and then sweet. You stay a long time.

choices.text: Write a letter at the host's table

effects.log: The ink is soft. The letter takes shape without effort.

choices.text: Pay the host with a stone

effects.log: They look at it, amused, and return it. "We take stories."

events.text: You tell the host a story, a true one, the kind you do not tell. The house hums, then shudders, then sets off at a walk. Dawn finds you on a new isle with a new view and a full heart. The host waves, small on the porch, from a distance.

choices.text: Wave back until the house is gone

effects.log: You feel lighter, as if a stone had been lifted off your chest.

choices.text: Look for the house on another night

effects.log: You find it twice more in your life, each time in the same warm dusk.

choices.text: Write the story down and keep it

effects.log: It reads better than you expected.

events.text: Once in a decade the moon-orchids of Iyo Isle bloom in a single night, and every botanist in the Isles crowds the terraces with lamps. A gardener, Sibyl Ann, saves you a stool and a thermos of plum-tea.

choices.text: Take the stool and wait

effects.log: The orchids sit in dark ranks, tight as fists.

choices.text: Ask what to look for

effects.log: "A change in the air," Sibyl says. "Like a held breath released."

choices.text: Help her tend the lamps

effects.log: It is warm work and the botanists make room for you.

events.text: At the third watch the first orchid opens, white and enormous, and a scent spreads that makes people laugh for no reason. Soon the whole terrace is bright with petals, and the botanists weep at the beauty.

choices.text: Breathe the scent deeply

effects.log: You laugh until your ribs ache, and feel years lighter.

choices.text: Sketch the bloom for the record

effects.log: Your sketch is rough and honest. Sibyl approves.

choices.text: Hold your breath out of caution

effects.log: You miss the effect, and the joke with it.

events.text: At dawn the petals fall, and Sibyl gathers them in a basket. She presses a single one into your hand, wrapped in paper. "It keeps for one night in ten years," she says. "Plant it in the right soil and a moon-orchid will grow in your garden."

choices.text: Plant it in your own garden

effects.log: Years on, a pale orchid blooms there on a moonlit night.

choices.text: Give it to a friend who is ill

effects.log: They smile at its scent and recover in a season.

choices.text: Pass it to Sibyl for the terraces

effects.log: She tucks it into the soil, humming.

events.text: A tortoise the size of an isle sleeps in the shallows off Muk Reach. Its shell is carved with maps of places that do not exist, and a young cartographer, Wen Torr, begs you to help her copy them before the tide covers the shell.
events.arc: The Jade Tortoise of Muk Reach

choices.text: Copy the maps with Wen

effects.log: Hours of ink and salt. Some of the places move while you draw.

choices.text: Ask the tortoise politely to hold still

effects.log: A slow eye opens. The shell stills for an hour.

choices.text: Warn Wen the tide is rising

effects.log: She hurries. The two of you finish ankle-deep.

events.text: The tortoise wakes at last and turns its great head. In a voice like wet stone it thanks you for copying what it dreamed, and gives you a single carved pebble from its shell. Wen weeps and swears to publish every map.
events.arc: The Jade Tortoise of Muk Reach

choices.text: Keep the pebble

effects.log: It points, faintly, toward places you have yet to visit.

choices.text: Give the pebble to Wen

effects.log: Her first atlas is dedicated to you.

choices.text: Set the pebble on the tortoise's brow

effects.log: The old creature sinks back to sleep, content.

events.text: A tiny isle drifts past your path with a single merchant on it, Cato Brill, who sells one item a year and refuses to say what. He waves you over for a visit and a cup of something warm.
events.arc: The Drifting Isle of a Single Merchant

choices.text: Hop across and visit

effects.log: The isle is the size of a courtyard and covered in teapots.

choices.text: Ask what he sells

effects.log: "Today? A reason," he says. "Wholesale only."

choices.text: Shout greetings from the bank

effects.log: He tips his hat. The isle drifts on.

events.text: Cato sells you a reason, in a jar, with a label that reads: for use when asked why. You open it later on a hard road and find a single true sentence that makes the road easier. You never learn who wrote it.
events.arc: The Drifting Isle of a Single Merchant

choices.text: Keep the empty jar

effects.log: It sits on your shelf, humming faintly.

choices.text: Pass the sentence on to someone who needs it

effects.log: They are quiet for a while, then thank you.

choices.text: Say it aloud on a high place

effects.log: The wind carries it. Somebody, somewhere, gets the reason too.

events.text: At Penumbra Quay, fishers launch lanterns at dusk to lure glowing sky-eels from the dark. A girl called Mei Sora hands you a lantern and tells you not to wish too hard, because the eels listen.

choices.text: Launch your lantern

effects.log: It rises, small and yellow, and the dark seems to lean closer.

choices.text: Whisper a wish anyway

effects.log: The lantern flickers, then burns stronger.

choices.text: Hold the lantern and say nothing

effects.log: Mei nods, as if you had passed some test.

events.text: A sky-eel rises to your lantern, vast and slow and glowing blue, and bows its head. It takes your wish, whatever it was, and carries it up into the dark. Mei says nobody ever hears whether it is granted. That is the point.

choices.text: Watch the eel out of sight

effects.log: The sky is quieter for it.

choices.text: Thank Mei and buy her a bowl of noodles

effects.log: She laughs. It is a good evening.

choices.text: Launch a second lantern for a stranger

effects.log: Somewhere a stranger's luck turns.

events.text: In the cellar of a closed tea-shop on Ninth Alley, you find a jar sealed with wax and a note: do not open until the world is ready. The shop's old widow, Madame Sol, says it has sat there for sixty years, and the world has not been ready yet.
events.arc: The Sealed Jar of Ninth Alley

choices.text: Ask Madame Sol what is inside

effects.log: "I never asked," she says. "That seemed rude."

choices.text: Hold the jar to your ear

effects.log: Something inside hums a single, careful note.

choices.text: Suggest leaving it sealed

effects.log: She is relieved. The jar stays in its cellar.

events.text: Madame Sol dies in her sleep that winter, and her will leaves the jar to you. You open it at last, on a clear spring morning, and out rises a small gold bird made of smoke that circles you once and flies away over the roofs of the alley. On the lid, in her hand: the world is ready now.
events.arc: The Sealed Jar of Ninth Alley

choices.text: Follow the bird to the end of the alley

effects.log: It leaves you at a crossroads with a feeling of being thanked.

choices.text: Pour tea at her shop in her memory

effects.log: The neighbours come. The shop is lively again for a day.

choices.text: Keep the jar as a reminder

effects.log: It sits empty on your shelf, faintly warm.

events.text: Under the Court archive lies a vault with one door and no lock, where the names of forgotten gods are kept. A clerk-spirit, Hanjae, tells you the vault grows heavier each year, as if the names missed being spoken.

choices.text: Ask Hanjae to open the door

effects.log: It swings wide with a sigh like a long-held breath.

choices.text: Offer a prayer at the threshold

effects.log: The air warms. A faint voice thanks you in a language you almost know.

choices.text: Ask who guards it

effects.log: "Nobody," says Hanjae. "We are not sure it needs guarding. We are sure it needs company."

events.text: Inside, ten thousand names hang from the ceiling on threads of silver light, each a small hum. When you walk among them they turn to follow you, shy as moths. Hanjae says a god forgotten for a thousand years may only be remembered by one voice.

choices.text: Speak one name aloud

effects.log: The thread brightens. Somewhere, far off, a shrine stirs in its sleep.

choices.text: Read the names silently

effects.log: A great number are of small hearth-gods, forgotten with their hamlets.

choices.text: Choose one at random and listen

effects.log: It carries a lullaby. You do not know whose.

events.text: The name you spoke belonged to Seolhwa, a snow-goddess of a valley now under water. A trace of her faith wakes in the vault and gathers at your feet, small and cold. Hanjae stares. No name has answered in a hundred years.

choices.text: Carry the trace to a shrine of snow

effects.log: The shrine lights. A thin frost-flower grows on its altar.

choices.text: Ask Seolhwa what she wants

effects.log: The trace swirls into a small, fierce shape and asks only to be remembered.

choices.text: Hold the trace until it fades

effects.log: It fades slowly, thanking you.

events.text: Word of Seolhwa spreads, and a trickle of pilgrims begins to visit her new little altar in the vault. Hanjae, flustered and proud, offers you the keys to the lock the door never had. "The vault wants a steward," the clerk-spirit says.

choices.text: Take the stewardship for a season

effects.log: You answer visitors, speak the names, and the vault grows lighter.

choices.text: Name Hanjae steward in your place

effects.log: The clerk-spirit weeps with joy and works through the night.

choices.text: Visit once a year and speak one name

effects.log: It becomes your small private rite, kept for centuries.

events.text: Beyond Cheonho's gate, in an unlit grove, stands a tree older than the pantheons: the Ur-Tree, from whose first leaf the earliest prayer was said. A caretaker, the dryad-spirit Soyul, will take you to see it if you promise not to pick a fruit.

choices.text: Promise and follow Soyul

effects.log: Her steps make no sound. The grove smells of cold iron and rain.

choices.text: Ask what happens if you pick one

effects.log: "The tree forgets who prayed to it," she says. "We would rather not."

choices.text: Hesitate at the grove's edge

effects.log: Soyul waits, smiling, with unhurried patience.

events.text: The Ur-Tree rises in the dark, vast and bare, its branches strung with faint lights, the first prayers of the first people. They are small: a harvest, a child, a lost goat. Soyul says they are the oldest faith there is, and also the strongest.

choices.text: Read the prayers on the lowest branches

effects.log: They are simple, tender, ordinary. You feel humbled.

choices.text: Add a prayer of your own to a bough

effects.log: The tree accepts it with a quiet rustle.

choices.text: Sit at the roots and listen

effects.log: A low voice hums in the wood. It is not a language so much as a mood.

events.text: A younger god of the Court arrives with a pruning saw and a decree. The Ur-Tree, he says, has grown too large and its faith leaks across too many domains. He means to cut it back. Soyul steps in front of him, very small.

choices.text: Stand beside Soyul and refuse him

effects.log: The young god pales. He had not expected a witness.

choices.text: Argue that pruning is not the Court's right

effects.log: You cite three charters. He leaves, muttering.

choices.text: Suggest he cut only the dead limbs

effects.log: It is a compromise. The Ur-Tree seems resigned.

events.text: At the close of the season the Ur-Tree puts out a single white blossom and lets it fall at your feet. Soyul says it has never done that for a god. The blossom does not wilt. It smells of the first rain.

choices.text: Keep the blossom on your altar

effects.log: Worshippers who see it grow quiet and kind.

choices.text: Plant its seed in a quiet corner of your domain

effects.log: A sapling grows, small and wise. Birds nest there.

choices.text: Return the blossom to the roots

effects.log: The Ur-Tree hums, and the grove brightens.

events.text: In the shadow of Daeak's great ridge lies the garden of Geumsan, a god who fell when his last worshipper died. A gardener-spirit named Pyo still tends it, trimming hedges for a god who will never walk its paths.

choices.text: Tour the garden with Pyo

effects.log: Every path is swept. Every bed is weeded. Nothing grows.

choices.text: Ask why Pyo stays

effects.log: "Someone must," Pyo says, "or he will have nothing left to come back to."

choices.text: Leave an offering at the gate

effects.log: A moth lands on it and does not leave.

events.text: At the garden's heart you find the dry basin of Geumsan's fountain, and in it a single coin, worn smooth. Pyo says the coin is the last offering anyone made him, and that if it were to be spent the god would be entirely forgotten.

choices.text: Ask what the coin was for

effects.log: A traveller once begged for a safe road. The road was safe.

choices.text: Add a coin of your own

effects.log: The fountain ticks like a clock restarting.

choices.text: Say a prayer of thanks for him

effects.log: The air clears. A single bird sings.

events.text: The garden begins to bloom out of season, one bed after another, and a pale figure takes shape among the roses. Geumsan, thin as smoke, asks Pyo in a whisper whether anyone has remembered him. Pyo nods, unable to speak.

choices.text: Tell Geumsan your name and domain

effects.log: He bows. His voice is a rustle of leaves.

choices.text: Offer him a place in your worship

effects.log: He accepts with grave courtesy.

choices.text: Stay silent and let Pyo have the moment

effects.log: The two embrace. You look at the roses until they are done.

events.text: Geumsan fades again with the first frost, but not as a fallen god: as a quiet one, content. Pyo invites you to a last cup of tea in the garden, now full of blooms. "He asked me to give you this," the spirit says, and hands you a pruning knife of old bronze.

choices.text: Take the knife and tend a garden of your own

effects.log: It cuts clean and never dulls. Your domain is a little greener for it.

choices.text: Hang it at the garden gate

effects.log: Visitors come, quietly, all year.

choices.text: Give it to Pyo for good

effects.log: Pyo weeps and works until sunset.

events.text: Prayers are going missing from the shrines of Baekun's lowland temples: spoken, then silent, never reaching the Court. The temple-keepers suspect a thief and ask you, a god with a keen ear, to find it.

choices.text: Take the case

effects.log: The temple-keepers press a ledger into your hands, relieved.

choices.text: Visit the nearest shrine at dusk

effects.log: A faint chill hangs near the altar, like breath on glass.

choices.text: Ask the temple-keepers who benefits

effects.log: They shrug. "Nobody we know. That is the worst part."

events.text: You wait in a shrine at midnight, and a small grey shape slips through the window, no bigger than a cat: a prayer-mouse, mouse-shaped and made of cobweb. It gathers the day's whispers into its paws and sets off.

choices.text: Follow it quietly

effects.log: It scurries through roof-gutters and under bridges, never looking back.

choices.text: Let it take one prayer, then speak to it

effects.log: It freezes, ears flat, utterly terrified.

choices.text: Set a small trap of sweet rice

effects.log: It sniffs, takes a grain, and does not take the bait.

events.text: The mouse leads you to a nest in the roof of a ruined temple, lined with a thousand prayers sorted by hope. A dozen mice sleep in a heap. Their leader, an old grey thing, says no god has listened to these prayers in years, so they listen instead.

choices.text: Take the nest's prayers up to the Court yourself

effects.log: You carry an armful. The Court processes them in a day.

choices.text: Tell the mice to bring the prayers back each dawn

effects.log: They nod. A strange partnership is born.

choices.text: Leave the nest alone and listen with them

effects.log: You spend an hour in the dark, reading hopes. It is humbling.

events.text: The prayer-mice become the temple's quiet couriers, and the lowland shrines fill with whisper-light. The old grey leader leaves you a thread of woven cobweb, strong as silk, that hums when someone prays your name.

choices.text: Keep the thread near your altar

effects.log: It trembles at odd hours. You answer every time.

choices.text: Give the thread to the temple-keepers

effects.log: They weave it into the temple bell-rope. The bell rings sweetly.

choices.text: Hang it above the nest as a thank-you

effects.log: The mice chitter happily.

events.text: Travellers speak of a shrine in Hwarin's ash-lands that burns day and night without fire: it glows, red and gold, and no heat comes off it. A pilgrim, Dae-ho, begs you to go with him, for his mother was a priestess there.
events.arc: The Shrine That Burned Without Fire

choices.text: Go with Dae-ho

effects.log: The road is grey and soft underfoot. He walks ahead, hands clasped.

choices.text: Ask what he hopes to find

effects.log: "Her last prayer," he says. "She never said it aloud."

choices.text: Send an offering ahead

effects.log: It vanishes in a single warm glow.

events.text: The shrine stands in a ring of ash, every pillar and rafter lit from within. Inside you hear a low chant, endless, unhurried, a congregation of voices singing a hymn that began before any of you were born. Dae-ho kneels and weeps.
events.arc: The Shrine That Burned Without Fire

choices.text: Kneel beside him and join the hymn

effects.log: It carries you. The words come as if remembered.

choices.text: Search the shrine for the priestess's place

effects.log: You find a small mat, still warm, and a folded cloth.

choices.text: Wait outside and let him be alone

effects.log: The glow plays on the ash like dawn.

events.text: On the mat lies a paper, the last prayer, written in a steady hand: not for herself, but for her son, that he find work he loves and a God who listens. Dae-ho reads it, and the glow brightens. The hymn changes key.
events.arc: The Shrine That Burned Without Fire

choices.text: Read the prayer aloud for him

effects.log: Your voice is steady. His is not.

choices.text: Answer the prayer in your domain's way

effects.log: The glow settles into a calm gold. The shrine seems to sigh.

choices.text: Say nothing and let the shrine do it

effects.log: The light wraps him. He bows his head.

events.text: The burning ends. The shrine stands cool and bare in the dawn, and Dae-ho, steadier, offers to keep it. You leave him a lamp, and a prayer-card with your own name written small. Weeks later it begins to glow warm in your pocket, and does not stop.
events.arc: The Shrine That Burned Without Fire

choices.text: Answer the prayer when it comes

effects.log: Dae-ho prays rarely and well. You never forget.

choices.text: Visit the shrine in spring

effects.log: It is garlanded. The ash-land has begun to green.

choices.text: Pass his prayers on to a temple nearby

effects.log: It spreads. The shrine has company.

events.text: The domain of Pungnyeon, god of harvest winds, has come unmoored: a whole province of golden fields now drifts slowly across the divine reach, trailing grain like smoke. Pungnyeon is nowhere to be found. The locals, shepherds of wheat, ask you to help.

choices.text: Offer to steer the province

effects.log: The fields tilt and creak under your feet. It is like riding a cloud.

choices.text: Ask the locals where Pungnyeon went

effects.log: They shrug. "On holiday, maybe. For three hundred years."

choices.text: Chase the province on a wind-horse

effects.log: You gallop beside it, laughing despite yourself.

events.text: You find Pungnyeon asleep in a barn at the heart of the drifting fields, an enormous, cheerful, hungover god snoring on a heap of grain. A single mouse has been fanning him with a feather for what looks like years.

choices.text: Wake him gently

effects.log: He blinks, sneezes a gale, and apologises to the mouse.

choices.text: Let him sleep and steer the fields yourself

effects.log: You learn their ways quickly. They like you.

choices.text: Pour him tea until he wakes

effects.log: It takes a week. He wakes smiling.

events.text: Pungnyeon wakes and is horrified. The province has wandered into the winter-lands, and the grain will not ripen in the cold. He asks you to carry a message to Saengmo's thaw-gods and beg a week of warm air.

choices.text: Carry the message at once

effects.log: The thaw-gods agree, amused, and send a gentle southern wind.

choices.text: Add a plea of your own to the message

effects.log: They laugh warmly. It works.

choices.text: Suggest Pungnyeon walk to ask in person

effects.log: He goes, grumbling, and returns with a basket of peaches.

events.text: The province drifts home on the warm wind and settles with a long sigh into the hills it left. Pungnyeon gives you a sheaf of gold wheat tied with red thread. "For your shrine," the god says. "It will never go to seed, and it will always feed someone."

choices.text: Set the sheaf on your altar

effects.log: Worshippers leave full-bellied after visiting it.

choices.text: Sow the grain on a barren plain

effects.log: In a season, green. In two, golden. A hamlet grows beside it.

choices.text: Give it to the mouse who fanned the god

effects.log: The mouse accepts it with a tiny bow.

events.text: A grey spirit arrives at your threshold, dripping though it has not rained. It introduces itself as Moon-Deok of the drowned pantheon, a god whose temple sank beneath a sea so long ago the sea has forgotten its name.
events.arc: The Visitor From a Drowned Pantheon

choices.text: Welcome Moon-Deok in

effects.log: It leaves a damp track on the floor and apologises for it.

choices.text: Ask what brings it here

effects.log: "A rumour," says Moon-Deok, "that someone up here still sets a place for the dead."

choices.text: Give it a dry cloth and a seat

effects.log: It is moved to tears of actual sea-water.

events.text: Moon-Deok tells of its pantheon: twelve gods who sank with their city when the tide rose, and who have been holding their breath ever since. It asks only that someone say their names, once, on dry land.
events.arc: The Visitor From a Drowned Pantheon

choices.text: Say the names with Moon-Deok

effects.log: Twelve names, one after another. The room fills with a faint, salt-smelling hum.

choices.text: Write them on a scroll for your altar

effects.log: The ink dries blue.

choices.text: Ask whether any might return

effects.log: Moon-Deok is silent. Then, softly: "One, perhaps."

events.text: As the twelfth name is spoken, a distant bell rings in the deep of your mind, and the room fills with the sound of surf. Moon-Deok stands very straight. A shape rises behind it, tall and robed in kelp, and bows to you with grave courtesy.
events.arc: The Visitor From a Drowned Pantheon

choices.text: Bow back and offer the guest-cup

effects.log: The robed god drinks. Moon-Deok sobs openly.

choices.text: Ask the robed god what it needs

effects.log: It needs a shrine, a single bell, and a few cheerful sailors.

choices.text: Offer a corner of your domain to the pantheon

effects.log: They accept, awed. It will be crowded.

events.text: The drowned pantheon takes root in a quiet cove of your domain, a small shrine of shells and sea-glass, and fishermen begin leaving offerings. Moon-Deok sends you a single pearl each spring, strung on a cord of kelp, with a note: thank you for the dry land.
events.arc: The Visitor From a Drowned Pantheon

choices.text: Wear the pearls as a token

effects.log: They warm when you are sad.

choices.text: Set them on the shrine's altar

effects.log: The shrine gleams. Fishermen pray more earnestly.

choices.text: Visit the cove at each tide

effects.log: Moon-Deok sits with you, damp and content.

events.text: Where Mongsa's dream-realm meets the waking sky, a market rises each night: stalls of sleep, hawkers of nightmares, a baker selling slices of lost afternoons. A stallholder named Ji-an offers to teach you to haggle in dreams.

choices.text: Learn to haggle

effects.log: Ji-an's method is to dream of a price and say it first.

choices.text: Browse the stalls

effects.log: A grey bird sells lullabies by the bottle.

choices.text: Ask what currency they take

effects.log: The stallholder wants memories, the small ones: a good breakfast, a pleasant hum.

events.text: A stall at the back sells nothing but a single blue lamp. The seller, a thin ancient god, says it holds one prayer that no god has been able to answer, and he will give it away free to anyone patient enough to listen to it.

choices.text: Listen to the lamp

effects.log: It hums a small, dry sorrow. You listen until it is finished.

choices.text: Ask the seller why he is selling it

effects.log: "I have carried it long enough," he says.

choices.text: Decline the gift

effects.log: He shrugs. "It will find someone."

events.text: The prayer in the lamp is a child's, from a hamlet that has been gone for a thousand years: please, let my brother come home. The brother never did. The lamp flickers with a hope that never learned to stop.

choices.text: Answer the prayer in the only way you can

effects.log: You pray back, softly, on the brother's behalf. The lamp stills.

choices.text: Seek the brother in the dream-realm

effects.log: You find a quiet man at a desolate crossing. He nods, as if he had been waiting.

choices.text: Burn the lamp gently in a shrine

effects.log: The light rises. The prayer is released.

events.text: The old god takes your hand, thanks you, and walks into the morning light with the blue lamp dark in his arms. Ji-an, who watched it all, hands you a small pouch of dream-dust. "On the house," the stallholder says. "For the rare customer who stays."

choices.text: Sprinkle the dust on your pillow

effects.log: You sleep a night of perfect peace.

choices.text: Keep it for a worshipper in need

effects.log: You give it years later to a woman in grief. She sleeps, at last.

choices.text: Sell a little at Ji-an's stall

effects.log: Customers love it. The stall flourishes.

events.text: In the storm-fields of Noegong, god of thunder, a gate of iron is bound with lanterns instead of chains. Each lantern holds a thunder-clap, saved up for a century. A watcher called Beom keeps them lit and begs for a sleep.

choices.text: Offer to watch the lanterns

effects.log: Beom stumbles off to bed with a tired smile.

choices.text: Ask what is behind the gate

effects.log: "The first thunder," says Beom. "It never learned to be quiet."

choices.text: Examine a lantern closely

effects.log: It shivers in your hand like a bird.

events.text: At the watch's end one lantern gutters, then goes out. The gate groans. Behind it something very large and very young turns over and begins, hopefully, to rumble. You can hear it asking to be let out.

choices.text: Relight the lantern

effects.log: The flame catches. The rumble subsides to a grumble.

choices.text: Speak softly to the gate

effects.log: The rumble pauses, curious.

choices.text: Wake Beom

effects.log: He staggers out, hair wild, and takes charge.

events.text: You bargain with the thunder: a single clap each year, at the festival of the first rain, in exchange for quiet. The thunder, delighted, agrees, and asks for rhythm lessons. Beom says in thirty years nobody has ever negotiated with it.

choices.text: Teach the thunder a drum rhythm

effects.log: It learns fast and very loud.

choices.text: Set the clap for the festival

effects.log: The calendar is amended and the annual clap becomes beloved.

choices.text: Let it clap once now to ease it

effects.log: The sky shivers. The clap is glorious.

events.text: The gate opens at last, not with a crash but a hum. The young thunder steps out, no longer feral, a great gentle rumble in the shape of a calf. It follows you home like a puppy and settles on the roof of your temple, where it rumbles contentedly at dusk.

choices.text: Keep the thunder as a guardian

effects.log: Worshippers feel safe beneath its low song.

choices.text: Let it roam the storm-fields with Beom

effects.log: They become fast friends.

choices.text: Name it and register it with the Court

effects.log: The Court is thrilled, then slightly alarmed.

events.text: In the cold deeps of Haeryong's sea lies a pearl the size of a temple, and inside it, say the divers, sleeps the first tide-wyrm. The sea-god has not woken it in ten thousand years. A diver named Mara-ni asks whether you will help her carry an offering down.

choices.text: Dive with Mara-ni

effects.log: The water is cold and brilliant. She leads by lantern.

choices.text: Ask why she wants to wake it

effects.log: "To say thank you," she says, "before I am too old."

choices.text: Prepare the offering on shore

effects.log: You braid kelp, shell and salt into a quiet gift.
