events.text: The pearl rests on a bed of white sand, ringed with the bones of drowned ships. It hums a single low tone. Mara-ni lays the offering at its foot and sings an old fishing song. The pearl glows, faintly, in answer.

choices.text: Sing along

effects.log: The song rolls out across the deep.

choices.text: Rest a hand on the pearl

effects.log: It is warm. Something inside turns over slowly.

choices.text: Back away respectfully

effects.log: You wait at a distance, watching it glow.

events.text: The pearl splits along a single clean seam, and a wyrm uncoils, vast, pale, impossibly young, its eyes full of old tide. It looks at Mara-ni, then at you, and bows its head to the sand in what looks like gratitude.

choices.text: Bow in return

effects.log: The wyrm exhales a stream of tiny silver fish.

choices.text: Ask what it wants

effects.log: It rumbles a single word: home. You understand.

choices.text: Offer it a place in your domain's waters

effects.log: It accepts with grave courtesy.

events.text: The wyrm swims out into the open sea and the tides turn in its wake, bright and clean. Mara-ni, old and shaking, laughs aloud. She hands you a single scale that fell as it rose, warm and silver. "It chose you to carry it," she says.

choices.text: Keep the scale near your altar

effects.log: It hums when storms approach.

choices.text: Give it to Mara-ni's grandchildren

effects.log: They shout with delight. The scale glows on their mantel.

choices.text: Set it as the keystone of a seaside shrine

effects.log: Fishers bless it. The sea is kinder there.

events.text: A golden boar roams the groves of Horang's foothills, and wherever it passes an oath cracks: a marriage vow, a treaty, a promise of friendship. The hill-gods are furious. A huntress, Yeon-ju, asks you to hunt it with her before more bonds break.

choices.text: Join Yeon-ju

effects.log: She hands you a spear of white ash and checks your boots.

choices.text: Ask what the boar wants

effects.log: "To be hunted," she says. "Nobody agrees why."

choices.text: Visit a broken oath first

effects.log: The two friends sit silent in a ruined arbour. You can feel the crack.

events.text: You track the boar through three days of fog, finding gaps in oaths along its path: a vow unkept, a bond frayed. At night you hear it grunting in the dark, huge and golden. Yeon-ju whispers that it has seemed lonely, lately.

choices.text: Set a trap of honeyed rice

effects.log: The boar sniffs and wanders off, offended.

choices.text: Wait in the open and let it come

effects.log: It stops ten paces away and stares. Its eyes are tired.

choices.text: Sing an oath of your own into the dark

effects.log: The boar tilts its head. It listens to the end.

events.text: The boar stands before you and you realise its tusks are the broken halves of a single sword, an oath-blade, shattered long ago. The boar is a kept promise made flesh, gone wrong because it was never fulfilled. Yeon-ju lowers her spear.

choices.text: Offer to fulfil the oath for it

effects.log: You learn the oath: guard a hill until a lost daughter comes home. You swear to find her.

choices.text: Hold the halves together until they mend

effects.log: The tusks fuse with a ringing note. The boar sighs.

choices.text: Ask Yeon-ju what an honest hunter does

effects.log: "Listens," she says. "Then decides."

events.text: You find the lost daughter's descendant, a grave old woman in a hill-farm, and bring her to the boar. She puts her hand on its brow. The tusks glow, the oath is fulfilled, and the boar lies down on the grass in a final peace.

choices.text: Build a small cairn where it lay

effects.log: Every spring flowers grow there.

choices.text: Take a single bristle as a keepsake

effects.log: It makes a fine charm against false oaths.

choices.text: Honour Yeon-ju at the hill-gods' meeting

effects.log: The gods are impressed. She is made a warden.

events.text: A hall on the edge of Unmyeong's fate-lands holds a thousand bells, each cracked, each hung for a god who fell. A bell-ringer called Sun-bi tolls them on the hour, and asks you to help on a night when the wind is wrong.

choices.text: Ring a bell with Sun-bi

effects.log: It cracks further with a dull, honest sound.

choices.text: Listen to the hall's hum

effects.log: A thousand notes, each slightly sour. It is strangely beautiful.

choices.text: Ask whose bells these were

effects.log: "Everyone's," Sun-bi says. "That is the point."

events.text: Among the bells hangs a newer one, still unspoiled, with a name on it: yours, or someone sharing it. Sun-bi pales. She says the bell was cast last year, and the only way to hang a bell is to know a god will fall.

choices.text: Ask Sun-bi to explain

effects.log: She says the Court forecasts falls by the quarter, to save the bell-casters time.

choices.text: Touch the bell

effects.log: It rings, clear and untroubled. No crack.

choices.text: Demand it be taken down

effects.log: Sun-bi refuses, then relents. She is frightened.

events.text: You confront the Court clerk who ordered the bell. He is polite and bored. "It is a prediction, not a sentence," he says. "Gods fall because of what they do. Yours has not yet been cracked." He leaves it hung.

choices.text: Vow to leave the bell unrung

effects.log: It hangs in the hall, silent as a held breath.

choices.text: Challenge the forecasting itself

effects.log: You file a formal complaint. It takes months.

choices.text: Ring it yourself in defiance

effects.log: It rings, perfect and unshaken. The hall falls silent.

events.text: Years later the Court abandons its forecasts, quietly, and Sun-bi lets the unspoiled bell hang in the front of the hall as a symbol: a bell that has never been cracked, because the god it was cast for never fell. It rings on festival mornings, and worshippers weep to hear it.

choices.text: Attend the ringing each year

effects.log: The note clears your mind.

choices.text: Give Sun-bi a gift for her long service

effects.log: She laughs and hangs it up beside the bell.

choices.text: Pass the tale to younger gods

effects.log: It becomes a cautionary fable and a comfort.

events.text: In the borderlands of Saengmo's domain, a grain grows only in frost, and the farmers say it feeds twice as well as summer wheat. A harvester, Ha-eun, shows you the ripening ears, silver and hard as bells.

choices.text: Taste a grain

effects.log: It is cold and sweet, like a winter morning.

choices.text: Ask how it grows

effects.log: "By being left alone," Ha-eun says. "Mostly."

choices.text: Help with the cutting

effects.log: The blades ring. By noon your hands are numb.

events.text: A warm wind comes early that year, and the frost-grain begins to rot on the stalk. Ha-eun and her neighbours stand in the fields, helpless. They have prayed to Saengmo for a cold snap, and no answer has come.

choices.text: Carry their prayer to Saengmo's court yourself

effects.log: You find the goddess in a garden, bewildered. She thought nobody grew grain in frost any more.

choices.text: Pray alongside the farmers

effects.log: Your voice joins theirs. The wind turns, faintly.

choices.text: Suggest cutting early and storing in snow-caves

effects.log: The harvest is saved in part.

events.text: Saengmo sends a cold wind down from her peaks, and the frost-grain stiffens and ripens. The farmers weep in the fields. Ha-eun brings you the first loaf baked from the saved harvest, hard and grey and warm from the oven.

choices.text: Share it with the farmers

effects.log: It is the best bread you have ever eaten.

choices.text: Leave a loaf at Saengmo's shrine

effects.log: The goddess smiles. The grain will thrive.

choices.text: Take a loaf home for your altar

effects.log: It does not stale. Worshippers marvel.

events.text: On the black ridge of Hwarin's fire-lands stands a choir of ash figures, singing without sound. Each is a priest who burned out serving the fire-goddess, and each still keeps its place at the altar. A warden, Gu-ri, asks you to help repair a fallen figure.

choices.text: Repair the fallen figure

effects.log: The ash is warm and light, like old paper.

choices.text: Listen to the silent song

effects.log: It is a hymn of thanks with no note of complaint.

choices.text: Ask Gu-ri who keeps them company

effects.log: "Nobody," she says. "That is why I stay."

events.text: The repaired figure opens its mouth and, for one note, sings out loud: a clear tenor, broken, grieved. The whole choir turns its head. Gu-ri drops her broom. They have not made a sound in four hundred years.

choices.text: Sing back to the figure

effects.log: Your voice joins its note. The choir shivers.

choices.text: Hold the figure's hand

effects.log: The ash is warm. You stay until dawn.

choices.text: Ask what it wants to say

effects.log: It tells you in a single phrase: I was proud to serve.

events.text: The choir sings at dawn, one by one, and the ash-lands ring. Hwarin herself comes down the ridge, tall and smoke-crowned, and listens until the last note. She bows to the choir and then to you. "These were my best," the goddess says, and the ridge is quiet.

choices.text: Bow in return

effects.log: Hwarin's attention warms you like a stove.

choices.text: Ask her to release them to rest

effects.log: She does, with a hand on each brow. They fall into ash and drift into the sky.

choices.text: Thank Gu-ri for her long watch

effects.log: Hwarin appoints her warden of the ridge for good.

events.text: An old man, Cheol-gi, arrives at your shrine on a cart pulled by a tired mule. He says he prays every night for his own god to retire, because the poor thing is exhausted, and wonders if you will pass the request along.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Prays for a God to Retire

choices.text: Take his request seriously

effects.log: He pats his mule with relief.

choices.text: Ask which god he means

effects.log: "The one who looks after my hamlet," he says. "She works too hard."

choices.text: Offer him tea and a bed

effects.log: He sleeps by the fire, hat still on.

events.text: You find Cheol-gi's god, a slight, cheerful goddess named Yun-seo, in a tiny temple on the edge of the wheat-fields. She has not slept in eighty years. Every prayer, every harvest, every sickbed in the valley falls to her alone.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Prays for a God to Retire

choices.text: Offer to take a share of the prayers

effects.log: She stares as if you had offered her a country.

choices.text: Tell her Cheol-gi worries about her

effects.log: She weeps, laughs, and weeps again.

choices.text: Arrange a rota with neighbouring gods

effects.log: It takes a week. It holds.

events.text: Yun-seo takes her first night off in eighty years, and the valley holds its breath. Nothing happens. The wheat grows. The children sleep. In the morning she wakes, startled, and Cheol-gi is at her doorstep with a flask of warm barley tea.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Prays for a God to Retire

choices.text: Stay for breakfast with them

effects.log: They talk about nothing for an hour. It is lovely.

choices.text: Slip away quietly

effects.log: The two do not notice.

choices.text: Make the rota official at court

effects.log: The Court approves, grudging and impressed.

events.text: In the cellar of an old exchange sits a chest sealed with a wax of debts. Nobody knows what it holds, only that everyone who opens it owes someone. A clerk, Ma-eum, asks you to help her appraise it for the Court.

choices.text: Help Ma-eum with the appraisal

effects.log: The wax is warm and sticky, and smells of old receipts.

choices.text: Ask how many have tried to open it

effects.log: "Seven," says Ma-eum. "All in debt now."

choices.text: Read the wax-seals

effects.log: Each seal is a promise broken, a price unpaid.

events.text: The wax lifts as you work, thread by thread, and the chest breathes out a smell of old paper and warm iron. Inside, a ledger, one page, lies open. It lists your name and a small sum, owed to a god you have never met.

choices.text: Ask who the creditor is

effects.log: Ma-eum checks, goes pale, and says the god is long dead.

choices.text: Offer to settle the debt in faith

effects.log: You pray for the dead creditor. The page glows.

choices.text: Tear out the page

effects.log: The ledger sighs. The sum is carried forward.

events.text: The debt is old, inherited with your domain, owed to the god who built your temple. The creditor's last request: that someone look after his orphaned shrine. It is crumbling, a day's walk south. Ma-eum offers to come along.

choices.text: Walk to the shrine with Ma-eum

effects.log: It is small, damp, and full of wrens. You repair the roof together.

choices.text: Send workers and pay the debt that way

effects.log: The shrine is restored within a season.

choices.text: Visit once a year to leave an offering

effects.log: The wrens expect you now.

events.text: Daeak's great peak is said to be a single breath of the first mountain-god, frozen in the moment it exhaled. Climbers of the gods' guild try to reach the summit and listen for the second half. A guide, Tae-yang, invites you to join.
events.arc: The Mountain That Was a God's Breath

choices.text: Join the climb

effects.log: The air thins and the mountain hums beneath you.

choices.text: Ask what they hope to hear

effects.log: "The inhale," says Tae-yang. "If it ever comes."

choices.text: Prepare the party's offerings

effects.log: You gather rice, salt, and a bell.

events.text: At the summit you press an ear to the cold stone and hear nothing, then a long, patient, almost imperceptible draw of air. The mountain is breathing in, very slowly, over a thousand years. Tae-yang falls to her knees.
events.arc: The Mountain That Was a God's Breath

choices.text: Breathe in with it

effects.log: You hold the breath until you feel it in your bones.

choices.text: Count its rhythm

effects.log: A breath every nine hundred years. You are on the edge of a miracle.

choices.text: Whisper thanks to the mountain

effects.log: The wind rises, once, in answer.

events.text: The inhale ends. A deep, enormous silence fills the summit, then the exhale begins, and the mountain trembles. Rocks sing. The clouds part. In the first light of the new breath, every god on the peak feels a small fear and a larger joy.
events.arc: The Mountain That Was a God's Breath

choices.text: Greet the new breath with a prayer

effects.log: It carries your voice a thousand miles.

choices.text: Help Tae-yang down in the shaking

effects.log: You carry her pack and her spirits.

choices.text: Stay on the summit until dusk

effects.log: The mountain settles to a new, softer hum.

events.text: A sleepless child at the edge of Mongsa's realm has not slept in nine days, and the dream-wardens have run out of lullabies. Her mother, a ferry-wife called Bo-ra, begs you to sing something new.

choices.text: Offer to try a lullaby

effects.log: Bo-ra weeps with relief and puts the kettle on.

choices.text: Ask what the child dreams of

effects.log: "Nothing," Bo-ra says. "That is what frightens her."

choices.text: Sit by the child's bed

effects.log: She watches you with huge, grave eyes.

events.text: You sing an old tune from your first shrine, and the child frowns. She says it is the wrong one. She hums another, odd and half-remembered, and you realise it is a lullaby from a pantheon that sank before she was born.

choices.text: Learn her tune and sing it back

effects.log: Her eyes close slowly. She is smiling.

choices.text: Ask where she heard it

effects.log: "In the dark," she says. "Someone sings to me."

choices.text: Hum with her till she sleeps

effects.log: It takes an hour. You are not sorry.

events.text: In the dream-realm that night you find the singer: a drowned goddess no one worships, stranded at the edge of sleep, who sings to sleepless children because no one will hear her otherwise. She asks, politely, for a shrine.

choices.text: Promise her a small shrine of reeds

effects.log: She weeps. The child sleeps well from then on.

choices.text: Bring her into your own pantheon

effects.log: You write her name in the Court registry. She is astonished.

choices.text: Ask her to sing for the whole ferry-town

effects.log: She does, and the whole town sleeps sweetly.

events.text: A tiger made of shadow stalks the groves below Horang's mountain, taking shadows from sleepers: they wake light-footed and strangely sad. The hill-folk ask you to hunt it, though they say it has never hurt anyone.

choices.text: Take the hunt

effects.log: The hill-folk press rice-cakes on you, grateful.

choices.text: Ask what a shadow is worth

effects.log: "Nothing," says a shopkeeper. "Until it is gone."

choices.text: Wait in the grove at night

effects.log: The wind drops. A hush falls.

events.text: The shadow-tiger pads out of the dark, vast and black and silent, and sits down in front of you. Its eyes are two small gold lamps. It lays a bundle of stolen shadows at your feet, neatly folded, and waits.

choices.text: Return the shadows to the sleepers

effects.log: Dawn finds the hamlet sleeping soundly, whole again.

choices.text: Ask the tiger why it takes them

effects.log: It cannot speak, but it leans against you and shivers. It is cold.

choices.text: Offer it a corner of your own shadow

effects.log: It accepts, purring like a kettle.

events.text: You bring the tiger to Horang's temple, and the mountain-god, stern and weary, recognises it at once: the shadow of his own first tiger, lost in a long-ago hunt. The great god kneels and the tiger presses its brow to his. Neither speaks.

choices.text: Leave them alone together

effects.log: You wait outside. The tiger does not return to the grove.

choices.text: Thank Horang for his patience

effects.log: He bows, which he never does.

choices.text: Ask whether the tiger may visit the hamlet

effects.log: Horang nods. It does, softly, on festival nights.

events.text: A forest in the shade of Mujin's tomb is full of stone statues, each a god who turned to stone rather than fall. A guide, Seo-hyun, leads tourists through for a few offerings. She says the statues sometimes whisper to the quiet.

choices.text: Join a tour

effects.log: The statues stand in meaningful poses. Some are crying.

choices.text: Ask Seo-hyun which are awake

effects.log: "The ones that listen," she says. "You can tell by the moss."

choices.text: Leave an offering at the forest gate

effects.log: A moth lands on it. A statue creaks.

events.text: You pause before a statue with moss-wet eyes, a god of small things whose name has been lost. As you stand there its lips seem to move: a whisper, faint as a leaf. It asks you whether the rain has come this year.

choices.text: Tell it the rain has come

effects.log: The moss brightens. The whisper thanks you.

choices.text: Ask it what it remembers

effects.log: It remembers a hearth, a child, a cup of milk.

choices.text: Brush the moss from its brow

effects.log: It sighs, like stone settling.

events.text: Seo-hyun admits the statues have not truly turned to stone: they are waiting. They will wake when someone remembers each name and says it in the forest, aloud. The nearest statue has been waiting a thousand years for yours.

choices.text: Learn the statue's name and speak it

effects.log: The stone warms. A hand lifts, slowly.

choices.text: Make a roll of all the names and read them

effects.log: It takes weeks. The forest stirs.

choices.text: Hire Seo-hyun to guide you on a yearly rite

effects.log: The rite becomes a custom, small and gentle.
